subject: Streaming UX — model fit, evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — streaming UX, model fit & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate you walking us through the streaming use case and how partial outputs surface in your UI. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What we heard:
- Primary objective: reliable streaming completion for clinical note snippets (3–10 sentences) with tight latency (p90 <= 350ms) and consistent stop behavior so the UI doesn’t show mid-sentence cuts.
- Current pain: occasional partial output coherence and missing stop sequence triggers when responses are streamed.
- Scale: ~200 concurrent writers during peak hours, target 5–10k requests/day initially.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
- Model candidates: test Llama-3-70B (base) and our quantized Redwood-70B-q4f16 variant for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Eval plan: run a 48-hour pilot against your prompt set for streaming scenarios (we’ll provide prompt-set-v2.jsonl).
- Streaming tweaks: use explicit stop sequences, streaming chunk_size=64 tokens, and enable prefix caching on repeated patient prompts.

Artifacts attached/linked:
- acme_health_streaming_eval_report.pdf (initial benchmark, small sample) — attachment stub
- prompt-set-v2.jsonl (prompt + expected completions) — attachment stub
- HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567
- Shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AbCdEfG/view

Proposed next steps:
1) If you’re comfortable, we’ll spin up a 48-hour pilot using the two model candidates and run your prompt set (no code changes needed on your side; we’ll stream via the Standard API).
2) Vivek (SE) will follow up with the recommended streaming config and a short checklist for front-end stop-sequence handling.
3) Confirm security questionnaire / DocuSign redlines so we can enable pilot-level access.

Can you confirm the pilot window and whether Priya should loop in procurement for contract redlines?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(attachment: acme_health_streaming_eval_report.pdf, application/pdf)
(attachment: prompt-set-v2.jsonl, application/json)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming UX, model fit & next steps

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- When you say "partial output coherence," we typically see the model stream a sentence and then produce a couple of tokens that aren't related (e.g., repeats or truncated phrases) before the stop. It looks like a buffering/early-flush issue in most cases.
- Latency: p90 <= 350ms is aggressive given our current infra; curious how Redwood achieves that consistently for 70B variants. Is that with batching disabled or some hybrid routing?

Yes, we’d like to run the 48-hour pilot. Priority items for us: 
- Updated prompt set (thanks for the v2 attachment)
- An example of the stop sequence config we should use in the client so we can test on our side as well
- A short write-up on how you’ll instrument streaming errors (so we can map to our front-end logs)

Priya — can you confirm whether procurement needs to be looped for a pilot order?

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Product Lead, Integrations
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming UX, model fit & next steps

Thanks Alex — good notes. Quick answers inline and next actions: 

- "Partial output coherence" — often a combination of early flushing and aggressive chunking. On Redwood we tune the chunk emit size and the stream buffer. For pilot we recommend chunk_size=64, buffer_timeout=30ms as a starting point.
- Latency baseline — our p90=~300–350ms for Redwood-70B-q4f16 in our Hosted environment with continuous batching disabled for low-latency routes; for Dedicated we can do better via pinned GPUs and tuned kernels. We’ll include the benchmark details in the report.
- Instrumentation — we’ll send a small tracing snippet that emits event types: STREAM_START, CHUNK_EMIT, STOP_MATCH, STREAM_END, and error tags for STOP_MISS / TRUNCATION. That will map to your existing logging.

Vivek — can you add the technical config + a short example prompt with stop sequences?

Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap — streaming UX, model fit & next steps

Alex / Priya — Quick tech note from the SE side based on your description and our initial sample runs: 

1) Model choice
- Start with Redwood-70B-q4f16 (quantized) for the pilot — best cost/latency balance vs straight Llama-3-70B. If quality regresses, fallback to Llama-3-70B or Redwood-70B-f16 for a second run.

2) Streaming config (recommended starting values)
- chunk_size: 64 tokens
- buffer_timeout_ms: 30
- stop_sequences: ["

", "
--END--", "
###"] (place explicit linebreak-based stop tokens in your render path)
- max_tokens_per_request: 256

Example prompt snippet (use SDK streaming):
--PROMPT_START--
System: You are a concise clinical summarizer. Do not hallucinate. Use plain sentences. Stop when you see the token "###".
User: Summarize the following notes into 3–5 sentences:
{patient_notes}
--PROMPT_END--

3) Instrumentation / telemetry
- Emit STREAM_START at request arrival, CHUNK_EMIT on each chunk, STOP_MATCH when stop sequence matched, STREAM_END on close. Add fields: model_variant, chunk_size, latency_ms.

4) Quick eval guidance
- Run 5k streaming samples, measure STOP_MISS rate, coherence score (human-rated), and p90 latency. We’ll run the same off our Hosted path for comparison.

Attached: prompt-set-v2.jsonl (small sample). I also exported a short eval report with a few example traces.

If you want, we can provision a pilot environment by Friday and share API keys scoped for the test.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: prompt-set-v2.jsonl, application/json)

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — streaming UX, model fit & next steps

Thanks everyone — this looks good. Procurement/proc steps: we can run the 48-hour pilot under our evaluation MSA; procurement will require a one-page SOW amendment and DocuSign. We can target a pilot start on Monday 2026-10-12.

Requests from our side before the pilot:
- Final prompt-set (we received v2, please confirm this is the full set)
- Short technical runbook for our front-end engineers describing the stop-sequence handling and the telemetry fields (STREAM_START, STOP_MATCH, etc.)
- Security questionnaire — we’ll send our questionnaire and will need SOC2 evidence for the pilot account.

Marissa — can you route the SOW and the DocuSign link? Vivek — please share the telemetry snippet and small client example (stop sequence handling) so our team can validate ahead of Monday.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Integrations, Acme Health
